### p158 A1

**German embassy address and Stumm signature, first printed part.**

**Literal header:** `A) YZ v LP (05.05 p.m., November 8th); 1331 (7/11) 2 TTLE; 1 TL RICHI-100`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DEUTSCHEBOTSAHAFTKONSTCNTINOPELXDNTERSCHRIOTSTUMMX
```

**Edited output — 4 observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
DEUTSCHEBOTSCHAFTKONSTANTINOPELXUNTERSCHRIFTSTUMMX
```

</details>

**Readable German:**

> Deutsche Botschaft Konstantinopel. Unterschrift Stumm.

**Conditional interpretation:** An embassy address with an explicit Stumm signature label. Four raw letter errors are repaired at their full coordinate cost.

The source supplies 100 native coordinates; the earlier OCR lost one, so its odd-length output is not used as the physical frame.

The raw BOTSAHAFT, KONSTCNTINOPEL, DNTERSCHRIOT letter errors are not source-transcription changes: the literal source remains fixed and all proposed replacements are priced in the edited layer.

The two printed A parts both contain address/signature language. Their headings are retained without inventing a distinct substantive payload.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov7-8-embassy-address-parts-scope-and-evidence"></a>

### Scope and evidence

Seven physical first/address parts on printed pp156 and 158 contain embassy,
legation or Etappe addresses and signatures. They are not seven recovered
substantive message bodies. Most headings announce additional parts that are
absent from the relevant section; the two printed p158 A parts themselves
both contain address/signature language.

The source edition has **568 native coordinate slots and 284 plaintext
positions**. Under the primary p156 A1 overstrike reading, all 284 positions
are fixed directly by the published key. Eleven observed-coordinate
substitutions produce the displayed ordinary-word proposals. There are no
insertions, exclusions, reorderings, source-mask fills or key changes. The
retained alternative p156 A1 glyph changes one raw letter and raises that
record's proposal cost from two substitutions to three.

| Record | Native slots | Raw fixed positions | Observed substitutions | Source fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| p156_A1 | 84 | 42/42 | 2 | 0 |
| p156_B1 | 80 | 40/40 | 0 | 0 |
| p156_D1 | 44 | 22/22 | 1 | 0 |
| p156_E1 | 78 | 39/39 | 0 | 0 |
| p158_A1 | 100 | 50/50 | 4 | 0 |
| p158_A2 | 106 | 53/53 | 2 | 0 |
| p158_B1 | 76 | 38/38 | 2 | 0 |

The three p162 D1 source masks receive independent character support from
these address witnesses; conversely, p162 D1's raw output supports all four
p158 A1 and both p158 A2 ordinary-word repairs. This is evidence for the
shared address formula, with different headers retained. It does not
establish identical missing payloads or a historical copying mechanism.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov7-8-embassy-address-parts-independent-address-witness-on-p162"></a>

**German embassy address with Bussche signature.**

**Literal header:** `A) YZ v LP (6.11 a.m., November 8th); FUER YZ 2200 (7/11) [2/3] TLE; 1 TL RICHI-84`

<details>

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
DEUTSCHEXBOTSCHAFTXKONSTANTIOPELXXBUSSCHEX
```

</details>

**Readable German:**

> Deutsche Botschaft Konstantiopel. Bussche.

**Conditional interpretation:** An address to the German embassy and a Bussche signature. The transmitted place-name lacks the second N of Konstantinopel and is preserved as Konstantiopel.

The two proposed ordinary-word repairs change DERTSCHE to DEUTSCHE and KSNSTANTIOPEL to KONSTANTIOPEL. The missing N is not inserted into the plaintext or the source.

The overstruck second character in the third group of source row 2 is transcribed X in the primary VXXVX reading. A V alternative, VVXVX, is retained independently; the alternative changes the raw H in DERTSCHE to X and does not establish a different historical message.

The faint part-count digit admits 2/3 readings. The header display uses editorial brackets to retain both alternatives; only the first part is printed in this section. The advertised 84-coordinate body length is clear and does not depend on that header digit. The Bussche signature is not expanded to a named historical person.

## p158 C2 — Notify GRUKONACH and telegraph the couriers arrival

**Edition context:** Munich couriers carrying radio operating documents.

**Related source pages:** [p151 D2](151.md#source-p151-d2), [p153 D2](153.md#source-p153-d2), [p153 E1](153.md#source-p153-e1), [p162 A1](162.md#source-p162-a1).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-munich-couriers-carrying-radio-operating-documents"></a>


[Source and certificate](../../experiments/courier_recovery/README.md)

Five records intercepted on 9 November concern couriers carrying radio operating documents to Munich: first parts p153 E1 / p162 A1 and continuations p151 D2 / p153 D2 / p158 C2. The best continuation fixes **67 of 68 positions** under the published Nov7–9 key; the damaged first part has a conditional 134-position reconstruction. The unit numeral remains **{5,6}** in the key, with a historical argument for **6** below.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

The first part is an editorial reconstruction with the source costs below:

**Readable German:**

> An Ingenieurinspektion Muenchen. Gefr. Geraus und Feldgr. Mahrer als
> Kurier mit Funkbetriebsunterlagen fuer Grukonach{5,6}02 7 Uhr abds.
> nach dort abgefahren.

The best-preserved second-part witness, p158 C2, reads directly without any
source-coordinate change:

**Readable German:**

> Grukonach{5,6}02 benachrichtigen. Eintreffen hierher drahten.
> Nachrchef 4 B 49909.

**Meaning:** The proposed first part tells the Engineer Inspectorate in
Munich that the two named men left at 7 p.m. as couriers carrying radio
operating documents for `GRUKONACH?02`. The continuation instructs the
recipient to notify that unit and telegraph the arrival back to the sender.

The names `GERAUS` and `MAHRER` remain unidentified; their U and H are not supported across every fit of both alignment models. The reading retains the unexpanded `FELDGR` and singular `ALS KURIER`.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-what-is-directly-supported"></a>

### What is directly supported

All three second-part records contain exactly 136 coordinates. Under the
known partial square, each fixes 67 of 68 plaintext positions. The p158 C2
text is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GRUKONACH?02BENACHRICHTIGENEINTREFFENHIERHERDRAHTENXNACHRCHEF4B49909
```

</details>

The p151 D2 repeat has `GRU1ONACH` at the beginning, and p153 D2 has
`BENACHWICHTIGEN`; the source edition preserves both. The unaltered p158
witness independently supplies the readable forms of both words.

The question mark denotes the observed pair **VF**, whose unassigned square value is **5 or 6**.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-a-separately-linked-conditional-reading-grukonach602"></a>

#### A separately linked conditional reading: GRUKONACH602

The [November 9 operational reports](166.md#edition-cases-military-nov9-operational-reports-historical-identification-most-likely-the-6th-reserve-division) use the same **VF** cell for a reserve-division numeral. A contemporary French telegram identifies the matching formation as the **6th Reserve Division**. Under that historical identification, **VF=6**, and both courier fields read **GRUKONACH602** with no additional source-coordinate changes.

This is one historical inference applied through a shared key cell. The base domain remains 5/6; the first-part reconstruction and its association with the continuation retain the assumptions below. The [context certificate](../../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json) records the external source, its date limits and the earlier p176b application.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-first-part-damage-and-explicit-reconstruction-cost"></a>

### First-part damage and explicit reconstruction cost

The first parts both advertise 268 coordinates but actually preserve 259
and 264 slots. Both visibly contain the six-letter group `VXDVDD`, which
the transcription retains. One overstruck glyph in p162 A1 is masked as a
source erasure; its displayed reading is kept separately.

Comparing the two sources without the key finds a five-slot relative gap:
all 260 possible gap starts were tested, and seven tied starts, 151–157,
leave only two known-coordinate disagreements. This does not locate the
other four slots missing from the longer witness.

For the **stated 134-position candidate**, exact alignment gives:

| Alignment model | p153 E1 | p162 A1 |
|---|---|---|
| Retain every source coordinate | Insert 9 slots; change 6 known coordinates; 32 tied minimum fits | Insert 4 slots; change 8 known coordinates; 2 tied minimum fits |
| Delete one received coordinate | Delete 1, insert 10; change 4 known coordinates; 192 tied minimum fits | Delete 1, insert 5; change 6 known coordinates; 14 tied minimum fits |

Every deletion position and tied optimum is retained. A fill of the overstruck p162 glyph is charged separately from observed-coordinate changes.

Within the first model, **123/134 proposed positions** have an unchanged coordinate pair in at least one witness for every combination of minimum fits. Requiring that support under both models gives **118/134**. These counts are conditional on the proposed wording and alignment families. The [certificate](../../experiments/courier_recovery/certificate.json) includes all raw masked-frame readings and exact costs.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-association-source-and-credit"></a>

### Association, source and credit

The two first-part records explicitly say first part of two, and all three
continuations say second part. The p153 D/E headers both read `RVV v N4` on
the same morning; the first-part `2120 (SY)` field also fits the p151 D
`SY v N4` continuation. Both bodies use the same unresolved `GRUKONACH?02`
field, and the instruction to report arrival follows naturally from the
departure notice. These facts support the association, but the typed log
does not explicitly cross-reference the parts as one original transmission.
The direct continuation remains readable independently of that association.

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, printed pp. 151, 153, 158 and 162 / PDF pp. 154, 156, 161 and 165,
in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [source inputs](../../experiments/courier_recovery/inputs.json) give
literal rows, headers and reproducible image rectangles. The Nov7–9 key
retains its historical and George Lasry / coauthor attribution in
[the key register](../../data/keys.json).

Source inspection, repeated-copy recovery, reconstruction and edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

```sh
python3 experiments/courier_recovery/build.py --verify
python3 experiments/courier_recovery/verify.py
```

## p158 — Routing and army-key instructions

**Edition context:** p158 — Composite routing and key instructions.

**Related source pages:** [p159 B](159.md#source-p159-b), [p159 C](159.md#source-p159-c), [p168 D](168.md#source-p168-d).

<a id="edition-cases-p158-p158--composite-routing-and-key-instructions"></a>



The historical p158 D record combines portions of two routing instructions under the published **Nov7–9** key. We identified its prefix with p159 B and its suffix with p159 C; repeated transmissions on p168 C/D support the component readings and several source repairs.

<a id="edition-cases-p158-most-likely-component-readings"></a>

### Most likely component readings

**Component B, from the p159/p168 witnesses:**

**Readable German — excerpt of the component reconstruction; bracketed expansions remain editorial:**

> Ueber 2. bayr. Gen.-[Kdo.], [Muenchen], an 7. [unit unclear] Div., [Landsberg an/am Lech]. Nicht durch Kabel. Armeeschluessel [doppelt]. Empfang [bestaetigen]. O.H.L. […] 11338 geh. […]

**Component C, from the p159/p168 witnesses:**

**Readable German — excerpt of the component reconstruction; bracketed expansions remain editorial:**

> Ueber 2. bair. Gen.-Kmd., Muenchen, an 4. bair. Div., [Innsbruck]. Nicht durch [Kabel]. [Armee-CHI] doppelt. Empfang [bestaetigen]. An O.H.L. […]

In both displays, `[…]` omits damaged or unexpanded administrative fields.
The exact component witnesses below retain their labels and positions.

**Meaning:** Route messages through the Bavarian command in Munich, onward to the indicated formations or destinations. Do not use cable transmission; apply the specified army-key treatment and acknowledge receipt.

The place-name expansions, unit labels and administrative fields remain partly conjectural. `Doppelt` concerns the army-key instruction discussed in the historical report below.

| Source layer | Slots | Optimal split | Edit cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Typed text | 232 | 130 | 19 |
| Typed text plus handwritten groups | 242 | 130 | 24 |

The 242-slot alignment has 222 exact known-symbol matches. Exhaustive comparison gives a unique split at 130 in the prefix/suffix model, across all eight combinations of source layers and ambiguous glyphs. Treating both glyphs as unknown retains that split, at costs 17 and 22 for the typed and augmented layers. The resulting correspondence identifies the components; the cause of their combination remains unknown.

<a id="edition-cases-p158-earlier-historical-reading-of-a-component"></a>

### Earlier historical reading of a component

Childs's report dated **20 November 1918**, printed on p42 of *German Military Ciphers from February to November 1918* (1935), deciphers order **11338**. Its SY→RVV via N4 header, 9 November date and 21:03 time agree with the p168 retransmission. [Primary report, p42](https://www.nsa.gov/Portals/75/documents/news-features/declassified-documents/friedman-documents/publications/FOLDER_268/41784789082381.pdf).

The report expands the garbled destination as `LANDWEHR REGIMENT; AN FECH`. The coordinate-derived `LA3DSBERGXAN0LECH` more closely suggests Landsberg an/am Lech; the exact expansion remains editorial. The surrounding report describes a separate **double-transposition army cipher**. It does not establish two complete ADFGVX encipherments.

The component bodies on **p168 C and D** are also discussed by **George Lasry,
Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker** in §6.4 of
[*Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of World War I*](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
printed p23 / author-PDF p24. That credit also applies to the parallel p159 B/C bodies. Their gloss describes doubled confirmation; the raw text distinguishes the doubled army-key instruction from receipt acknowledgment.

The p158 composite identification and repair audit are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026**. The [historical comparison](../../data/reviews/historical_component_prior.json) records the earlier readings.

The [full p168 C witness](168.md#edition-cases-radio-p168-munich-routing-witness) resolves the six-coordinate/four-coordinate group alignment. Its conditional frame fixes 139/140 raw positions, and an observed `V` from p159 B supplies the last coordinate. Twelve ownership aliases yield the same completed stream. The observed p168 pair `VG = K` also supports `GEN KDO`: adopting its G at p159 source 169 costs one `X→G` substitution, changing the H in `GEN HDO` above.


<details>
<summary>Comparative source sections from other printed pages</summary>

### Component readings

The p159 B frame has a duplicated five-coordinate group, a missing group, two erased coordinates and a source disagreement. In p159 C, comparison with the repeat reduces a six-coordinate group to five. Three edited component versions re-encrypt exactly using the established square cells, with the digit pair 5/6 unresolved. The [certificate](../../data/certificates/p158.json) records the repairs and raw readings.

## p158 E1 — Serbian cavalry and northward departure: another source witness

**Edition context:** November 8: a separate Serbian-cavalry report witness.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov8-serbian-cavalry-parallel-november-8-a-separate-serbian-cavalry-report-witness"></a>


Source review and editorial work: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Published
Nov7–9 key: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker; unchanged
here. The operational body and p170 word proposals were already edited in
[the p166/p167/p170 report study](166.md#edition-cases-military-nov9-operational-reports). This addition · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)
is a new physical witness and source-alignment audit, not a claim to a new
body decipherment or universal priority.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p158_E_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov8_serbian_cavalry_parallel/sources/p158_E_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
<a id="edition-cases-military-nov8-serbian-cavalry-parallel-conditional-shared-digits"></a>

### Conditional shared digits

**Readable German — conditional shared digits, with the existing source edition retained:**

> ANENMELDUNG. Serb. Kavallerie Peterwadein und Fehertemplom eingerueckt. Abmarsch 217 I D und 6 R D nach Norden ohne Feinberuehrung.

The [shared-reference assignment](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) supplies **VF=6** to the unchanged division pair, completing **118/118** labels in the selected word edition. The five observed substitutions and one source-linked added A are unchanged; the opposite square retains 5. This propagates a separately justified digit to this physical witness and does not count the earlier p170 unit identification again.


<a id="edition-cases-military-nov8-serbian-cavalry-parallel-what-the-additional-source-establishes"></a>

### What the additional source establishes

Printed p158 E1 has **235 coordinates against an advertised 236**. Its
third source row contains the four-coordinate group `XDGV`. The independent
p170 B1 copy has `AXDGV` in the corresponding position. Adding its observed
`A` restores a 236-coordinate frame while retaining all 235 p158 coordinates
in their printed order. The source-linked frame fixes **117 of 118
plaintext positions** and preserves three letter disagreements with p170.

The report describes Serbian cavalry entering the places transmitted as
`PETERWADEIN` and `FEHERTEMPLOM`, followed by a northward departure of
`217 I D` and `? R D`. The spelling `PETERWADEIN` lacks the R in the fuller
place-name used by another report. The final `FEINBERUEHRUNG` appears to
mean enemy contact but lacks the D of `FEIND`; the exact readable stream
retains both omissions. `ANENMELDUNG` remains unexpanded.

The conservative edited layer uses **five observed-coordinate
substitutions**: three are supported by the independent raw copy; two are
shared ordinary-word repairs. The added A is separately priced as **one
source-linked coordinate addition**, not represented as a coordinate
visible on p158. No source coordinate is excluded, reordered or masked.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov8-serbian-cavalry-parallel-the-two-literal-headers"></a>

### The two literal headers

| Witness | Printed header |
|---|---|
| p158 E1 | `E) UKS v ZON (11.44 p.m., November 8th); 1915 (8/11) 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-236; following control: ZON UM; page footer: (continued)` |
| p170 B1 | `UKS v ZON (11.44 p.m., November 9th); 1915 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-236` |

The same station pair, reception time and `1915` field recur. The reception
dates differ by one day, and p158 also supplies `(8/11)`. These observations
support a repeated body; they do not identify a specific copying or
reception mechanism. The p158 heading advertises two parts, but this edition
adds only the first. The next page's separate header is not silently joined
to it as its second part.

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels preserved:**

> ANENMELDUNG. Serb. Kavallerie Peterwadein und Fehertemplom eingerueckt. Abmarsch 217 I D und ? R D nach Norden ohne Feinberuehrung.

**Conditional interpretation:** Serbian cavalry is reported as having
entered the two transmitted place-names. A northward departure of the
labelled formations follows. Reading the final phrase as “without enemy
contact” requires recognizing the missing D in the transmitted word; that
is a prose interpretation, not an extra recovered coordinate. The earlier
report study gives fuller place-name and operational context separately.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov8-serbian-cavalry-parallel-what-the-independent-copy-supports"></a>

### What the independent copy supports

The p170 B1 raw source directly supports three p158 changes:

| Plaintext position | p158 source-linked raw | p170 raw | Proposed label |
|---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 26 | T | E | E |
| 36 | 2 | I | I |
| 96 | Y | R | R |

Those supply the E of `KAVALLERIE`, the I of the transmitted
`PETERWADEIN`, and the R of `NORDEN`. Both copies share raw
`EINGSRUECKT` and `FEINBELUEHRUNG`; their E/R corrections therefore remain
editorial and are not presented as independently corroborated letters.

Keeping both source values at every disagreement gives a conservative
**114/118-position** common template:

**Conditional interpretation — union of the two raw-source domains:**

```text
ANENMELDUNGXSERBXKAVALLERI?PETERWADE?NUNDFEHERTEMPLOMEINGSRUECKTXXABMARSCH217XIXDXUND?XRXDNACHNO?DENOHNEFEINBELUEHRUNG
```

Its per-position union domains are recorded in the certificate. Agreement
on a repeated body does not erase the disagreements between the two
physical witnesses.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov8-serbian-cavalry-parallel-every-one-coordinate-alignment"></a>

### Every one-coordinate alignment

The verifier compares the 235 observed p158 coordinates with all **236**
possible one-coordinate omissions from the complete p170 source. This
comparison uses the two printed ciphertexts, with no desired plaintext or
language score.

| Source boundary receiving the parallel A | Observed agreements | Observed disagreements | Filled 236-coordinate stream |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 82 | 232 | 3 | Same as the other minima |
| 83 | 232 | 3 | Same as the other minima |
| 84 | 232 | 3 | Same as the other minima |
| 85 | 232 | 3 | Same as the other minima |

The A run makes all four placements equivalent after the coordinate is
supplied. Their raw unfilled outputs and source maps differ, and all are
retained. Boundary 85 is the primary display because it places the extra
coordinate at the start of the visibly short group. It is not a uniquely
recovered historical omission site. All prices and all frames within one
disagreement of the minimum are included in the certificate.

the native p158 groups, both headers, the source-linked addition, the
unchanged key and prior credits. The
[certificate](../../experiments/nov8_serbian_cavalry_parallel/certificates.json)
retains the native odd diagnostic, every gap price, competing source maps,
all edits, source-supported and shared-editorial letters, union domains and
both globally consistent 5/6 completions. Each complete square exactly
decrypts and re-encrypts the raw, edited, optional-headline and prior frames.
Neither completion is selected historically by this edition.

The existing p170 source record is hash-bound and its image has been
reviewed independently. Both its crop and the new p158 crop are checked by
exact RGB regeneration from the pinned Childs PDF. The
[README](../../experiments/nov8_serbian_cavalry_parallel/README.md) gives the
